The Company may redeem some or all of its Senior Unsecured Notes prior to their maturity at redemption prices based on a premium, plus accrued and unpaid interest as described in the indentures governing the Senior Unsecured Notes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;On February 14, 2022, the Company redeemed all of the $104.8&#160;million of aggregate principal amount outstanding of its 5.0% Senior Notes due 2024 (&#x201c;2024 Senior Notes&#x201d;), with cash on hand, pursuant to the terms of the indenture governing the 2024 Senior Notes which provided for a redemption price equal to 100 percent of the principal amount of the 2024 Senior Notes on the date of redemption, plus accrued and unpaid interest.  The Company canceled all redeemed 2024 Senior Notes upon settlement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;On June&#160;23, 2021, the Company issued $400.0&#160;million in aggregate principal amount of its 6.5% Senior Notes at par with a maturity date of July&#160;15, 2028 (&#x201c;2028 Senior Notes&#x201d;).  The Company received net proceeds of $392.8&#160;million after deducting fees of $7.2&#160;million, which are being amortized as deferred financing costs over the life of the 2028 Senior Notes.  The net proceeds were used to repurchase $193.1&#160;million and $172.3&#160;million of outstanding principal amount of the Company&#x2019;s 6.125% Senior Notes due 2022 (&#x201c;2022 Senior Notes&#x201d;) and 2024 Senior Notes, respectively, through a cash tender offer (&#x201c;Tender Offer&#x201d;), and to redeem the remaining $19.3&#160;million of 2022 Senior Notes not repurchased as part of the Tender Offer (&#x201c;2022 Senior Notes Redemption&#x201d;).  The Company paid total consideration, excluding accrued interest, of $385.3&#160;million, and recorded a net loss on extinguishment of debt of $2.1&#160;million for the three months ended June 30, 2021, which included $1.5&#160;million of accelerated unamortized deferred financing costs and $0.6&#160;million of net premiums.  The Company canceled all repurchased and redeemed 2022 Senior Notes and 2024 Senior Notes upon settlement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Please refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 5 - Long-Term Debt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;&lt;a href="http://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/893538/000089353822000020/sm-20211231.htm" style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;2021 Form 10-K&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; for additional detail on the Company&#x2019;s Senior Notes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Covenants&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;As discussed above, the Company is subject to certain financial and non-financial covenants under the Credit Agreement and under the indentures governing the Senior Notes that, among other terms, limit the Company&#x2019;s ability to incur additional indebtedness, make restricted payments including dividends and common stock repurchases, sell assets, create liens that secure debt, enter into transactions with affiliates, merge or consolidate with other entities, and with respect to the Company&#x2019;s restricted subsidiaries, permit the consensual restriction on the ability of such restricted subsidiaries to pay dividends or indebtedness owing to the Company or to any other restricted subsidiaries.  The Company was in compliance with all financial and non-financial covenants as of September 30, 2022, and through the filing of this report.  Please refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 5 - Long-Term Debt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;&lt;a href="http://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/893538/000089353822000020/sm-20211231.htm" style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;2021 Form 10-K&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; for additional detail on the Company&#x2019;s covenants under the indentures governing the Senior Notes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Capitalized Interest&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Capitalized interest costs for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, totaled $5.1&#160;million and $3.5&#160;million, respectively, and totaled $12.3&#160;million and $12.5&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, respectively. During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and through the filing of this report, the Company amended certain of its drilling rig contracts resulting in the increase of day rates and potential early termination fees, and the extension of contract terms.  As of the filing of this report, the Company&#x2019;s drilling rig commitments totaled $32.8 million under contract terms extending through the third quarter of 2023.  If all of these contracts were terminated as of the filing of this report, the Company would avoid a portion of the contractual service commitments; however, the Company would be required to pay $19.6 million in early termination fees.  No early termination penalties or standby fees were incurred by the Company during the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and the Company does not expect to incur material penalties with regard to its drilling rig contracts during the remainder of 2022.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Drilling and Completion Commitments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;.  During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, the Company entered into an agreement that includes minimum drilling and completion footage requirements on certain existing leases.  If these minimum requirements are not satisfied by March&#160;31, 2024, the Company will be required to pay liquidated damages based on the difference between the actual footage drilled and completed and the minimum requirements.  As of September&#160;30, 2022, the liquidated damages could range from zero to a maximum of $74.5&#160;million, with the maximum exposure assuming no additional development activity occurred prior to March&#160;31, 2024.  As of the filing of this report, the Company expects to meet its obligations under this agreement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Contingencies&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company is subject to litigation and claims arising in the ordinary course of business.  The Company accrues for such items when a liability is both probable and the amount can be reasonably estimated.  In the opinion of management, the anticipated results of any pending litigation and claims are not expected to have a material effect on the results of operations, the financial position, or the cash flows of the Company.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock>

    <us-gaap:CompensationAndEmployeeBenefitPlansTextBlock
      contextRef="i3b79dc1c07344b1a997ff668145f5bfb_D20220101-20220930"
      id="id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82MS9mcmFnOjhmNTQ5NGMxYWY3NDRkMmNiYTI4YWIwMzNkNzk1OTk0L3RleHRyZWdpb246OGY1NDk0YzFhZjc0NGQyY2JhMjhhYjAzM2Q3OTU5OTRfNzc4MQ_802c621e-90bc-4ac6-8494-0019317f1119">&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 7 - Compensation Plans&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;As of September&#160;30, 2022, 3.8&#160;million shares of common stock were available for grant under the Company&#x2019;s Equity Incentive Compensation Plan (&#x201c;Equity Plan&#x201d;).  The Company may also grant other types of long-term incentive-based awards, such as cash awards and performance-based cash awards, to eligible employees.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Performance Share Units&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company has granted performance share units (&#x201c;PSU&#x201d; or &#x201c;PSUs&#x201d;) to eligible employees as part of its Equity Plan.  The number of shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock issued to settle PSUs ranges from zero to two times the number of PSUs awarded and is determined based on certain criteria over a &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82MS9mcmFnOjhmNTQ5NGMxYWY3NDRkMmNiYTI4YWIwMzNkNzk1OTk0L3RleHRyZWdpb246OGY1NDk0YzFhZjc0NGQyY2JhMjhhYjAzM2Q3OTU5OTRfNjQw_da831adf-7494-4b6e-83bc-d536911b4763"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;-year performance period.  PSUs generally vest on the third anniversary of the date of the grant or upon other triggering events as set forth in the Equity Plan.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;For PSUs granted in 2019, which the Company determined to be equity awards, the settlement criteria included a combination of the Company&#x2019;s Total Shareholder Return (&#x201c;TSR&#x201d;) relative to the TSR of certain peer companies and the Company&#x2019;s cash return on total capital invested (&#x201c;CRTCI&#x201d;) relative to the CRTCI of certain peer companies over the associated &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82MS9mcmFnOjhmNTQ5NGMxYWY3NDRkMmNiYTI4YWIwMzNkNzk1OTk0L3RleHRyZWdpb246OGY1NDk0YzFhZjc0NGQyY2JhMjhhYjAzM2Q3OTU5OTRfMTE1Mw_da831adf-7494-4b6e-83bc-d536911b4763"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;-year performance period.  In addition to these performance criteria, the award agreements for these grants also stipulated that if the Company&#x2019;s absolute TSR was negative over the &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82MS9mcmFnOjhmNTQ5NGMxYWY3NDRkMmNiYTI4YWIwMzNkNzk1OTk0L3RleHRyZWdpb246OGY1NDk0YzFhZjc0NGQyY2JhMjhhYjAzM2Q3OTU5OTRfMTMzNA_da831adf-7494-4b6e-83bc-d536911b4763"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;-year performance period, the maximum number of shares of common stock that could be issued to settle outstanding PSUs was capped at one times the number of PSUs granted on the award date, regardless of the Company&#x2019;s TSR and CRTCI performance relative to its peer group.  The fair value of the PSUs granted in 2019 was measured on the grant date using the GBM Model, with the assumption that the associated CRTCI performance condition would be met at the target amount at the end of the performance period.  Compensation expense for PSUs is recognized within general and administrative expense and exploration expense over the vesting periods of the respective awards.  PSUs granted in 2019 vested during the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and earned a 2.0 times multiplier upon settlement.  The Company and all eligible recipients mutually agreed to net share settle a portion of the vested awards to cover income and payroll tax withholdings, as provided for in the Equity Plan and the award agreement.  After withholding 349,487 shares to satisfy income and payroll tax withholding obligations, 654,923 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock were issued in accordance with the terms of the award agreement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;For PSUs granted in 2022, which the Company determined to be equity awards, settlement will be determined based on a combination of the following criteria measured over the &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82MS9mcmFnOjhmNTQ5NGMxYWY3NDRkMmNiYTI4YWIwMzNkNzk1OTk0L3RleHRyZWdpb246OGY1NDk0YzFhZjc0NGQyY2JhMjhhYjAzM2Q3OTU5OTRfNTQ5NzU1ODM1MzQw_da831adf-7494-4b6e-83bc-d536911b4763"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;-year performance period: the Company&#x2019;s TSR relative to the TSR of certain peer companies, the Company&#x2019;s absolute TSR, free cash flow (&#x201c;FCF&#x201d;) generation, and the achievement of certain ESG targets, in each case as defined by the award agreement.  The absolute and relative TSR portions of the fair value of the PSUs granted in 2022 &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;were measured on the grant date using the GBM Model.  The portion of the awards associated with FCF generation and ESG performance conditions assumes that target amounts will be met at the end of the performance period.  Compensation expense for PSUs is recognized within general and administrative expense and exploration expense over the vesting periods of the respective awards.  The Company initially records compensation expense associated with the issuance of PSUs based on the fair value of the awards as of the date of grant.  As these awards depend on a combination of performance-based settlement criteria and market-based settlement criteria, compensation expense may be adjusted in future periods as the number of units expected to vest increases or decreases based on the Company&#x2019;s expected FCF generation and achievement of certain ESG targets.  During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, the Company granted a total of 276,010 PSUs with a grant date fair value of $7.4 million.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Total compensation expense recorded for PSUs was $0.6&#160;million and $0.8&#160;million for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, respectively, and $2.0&#160;million and $5.3&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, respectively.  As of September&#160;30, 2022, there was $6.8 million of total unrecognized compensation expense related to non-vested PSUs, which is being amortized through mid-2025.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;A summary of activity during the nine style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:5.85pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-3.15pt;vertical-align:baseline"&gt;(1)&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The number of shares of common stock assumes a multiplier of one.  The actual number of shares of common stock to be issued will range from zero to two times the number of PSUs awarded depending on the &lt;span style="-sec-ix-hidden:id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82MS9mcmFnOjhmNTQ5NGMxYWY3NDRkMmNiYTI4YWIwMzNkNzk1OTk0L3RleHRyZWdpb246OGY1NDk0YzFhZjc0NGQyY2JhMjhhYjAzM2Q3OTU5OTRfNTQ5NzU1ODMxODg5_da831adf-7494-4b6e-83bc-d536911b4763"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;-year performance multiplier.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Employee Restricted Stock Units&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company has granted restricted stock units (&#x201c;RSU&#x201d; or &#x201c;RSUs&#x201d;) to eligible employees as part of its Equity Plan.  Each RSU granted represents a right to receive one share of the Company&#x2019;s common stock upon settlement of the award at the end of the specified vesting period.  RSUs generally vest in one-third increments on each anniversary date of the grant over the applicable vesting period or upon other triggering events as set forth in the Equity Plan.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company records compensation expense associated with the issuance of RSUs based on the fair value of the awards as of the date of grant.  The fair value of an RSU is equal to the closing price of the Company&#x2019;s common stock on the date of the grant.  Compensation expense for RSUs is recognized within general and administrative expense and exploration expense over the vesting periods of the respective awards.  During the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, the Company granted to employees a total of 526,776 RSUs with a grant date fair value of $18.0 million, and the Company settled RSUs upon the vesting of awards granted in previous years.  The Company and all eligible recipients mutually agreed to net share settle a portion of the vested awards to cover income and payroll tax withholdings, as provided for in the Equity Plan and applicable award agreements.  After withholding 284,423 shares to satisfy income and payroll tax withholding obligations, 636,504 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock were issued in accordance with the terms of the applicable award agreements during the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Total compensation expense recorded for RSUs was $3.5&#160;million and $2.9&#160;million for the three months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, respectively, and $10.0&#160;million and $7.2 million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, respectively.  As of September&#160;30, 2022, there was $27.8&#160;million of total unrecognized compensation expense related to non-vested RSUs, which is being amortized through mid-2025.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:3pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, the Company issued a total of 29,471 and 57,795 shares, respectively, of its common stock as compensation to its non-employee directors under the Equity Plan.  Shares issued during 2022 will fully vest on December&#160;31, 2022, and shares issued during 2021 fully vested on December&#160;31, 2021.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Employee Stock Purchase Plan&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Under the Company&#x2019;s Employee Stock Purchase Plan (&#x201c;ESPP&#x201d;), eligible employees may purchase shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock through payroll deductions of up to 15 percent of eligible compensation, subject to a maximum of 2,500 shares per offering period and a maximum of $25,000 in value related to purchases for each calendar year.  The purchase price of the common stock is 85 percent of the lower of the trading price of the common stock on either the first or last day of the six-month offering period.  The ESPP is intended to qualify as an &#x201c;employee stock purchase plan&#x201d; under Section 423 of the Internal Revenue Code.  There were a total of 65,634 and 252,665 shares issued under the ESPP during the nine months ended September 30, 2022, and 2021, respectively.  Total proceeds to the Company for the issuance of these shares was $1.6&#160;million and $1.3&#160;million for the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, respectively.  The fair value of ESPP grants is measured at the date of grant using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Please refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 7 - Compensation Plans&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;&lt;a href="http://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/893538/000089353822000020/sm-20211231.htm" style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;2021 Form 10-K&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; for additional detail on the Company&#x2019;s Equity Plan.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:CompensationAndEmployeeBenefitPlansTextBlock>

This guidance defines fair value as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.  Market or observable inputs are the preferred sources of values, followed by assumptions based on hypothetical transactions in the absence of market inputs.  The fair value hierarchy for grouping these assets and liabilities is based on the significance level of the following inputs:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div liabilities, quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are not active, and model-derived valuations whose inputs are observable or whose significant value drivers are value hierarchy based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.  The following is a description of the valuation methodologies used by the Company as well as the general classification of such instruments pursuant to the above fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Derivatives&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company uses Level 2 inputs to measure the fair value of oil, gas, and NGL commodity derivatives.  Fair values are based upon interpolated data.  The Company derives internal valuation estimates taking into consideration forward commodity price curves, counterparties&#x2019; credit ratings, the Company&#x2019;s credit rating, and the time value of money.  These valuations are then compared to the respective counterparties&#x2019; mark-to-market statements.  The considered factors result in an estimated exit price that management believes provides a reasonable and consistent methodology for valuing derivative instruments.  The commodity derivative instruments utilized by the Company are not considered by management to be complex, structured, or illiquid.  The oil, gas, and NGL commodity derivative markets are highly active.  Please refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;in this report, and to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 8 - Fair Value Measurements &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;&lt;a href="http://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/893538/000089353822000020/sm-20211231.htm" style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;2021 Form 10-K&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;     <us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy
      contextRef="i3b79dc1c07344b1a997ff668145f5bfb_D20220101-20220930"
      id="id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV82Ny9mcmFnOjBjOWMxNTk5YzE2ZTQ0MmJhNmUzOTQ5MjE3MTk0ZDE2L3RleHRyZWdpb246MGM5YzE1OTljMTZlNDQyYmE2ZTM5NDkyMTcxOTRkMTZfMzYxNw_9f743618-1c8f-4cf4-ac6f-a0f53f490e3a">&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Derivatives&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company uses Level 2 inputs to measure the fair value of oil, gas, and NGL commodity derivatives.  Fair values are based upon interpolated data.  The Company derives internal valuation estimates taking into consideration forward commodity price curves, counterparties&#x2019; credit ratings, the Company&#x2019;s credit rating, and the time value of money.  These valuations are then compared to the respective counterparties&#x2019; mark-to-market statements.  The considered factors result in an estimated exit price that management believes provides a reasonable and consistent methodology for valuing derivative instruments.  The commodity derivative instruments utilized by the Company are not considered by management to be complex, structured, or illiquid.  The oil, gas, and NGL commodity derivative markets are highly active.  Please refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;in this report, and to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 8 - Fair Value Measurements &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;&lt;a href="http://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/893538/000089353822000020/sm-20211231.htm" style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;2021 Form 10-K&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; for more information regarding the Company&#x2019;s derivative instruments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy>

Diluted net income or loss per common share is calculated by dividing net income or loss available to common stockholders by the diluted weighted-average number of common shares outstanding, which includes the effect of potentially dilutive securities.  Potentially dilutive securities for this calculation consist primarily of non-vested RSUs, contingent PSUs, and Warrants, all of which were measured using the treasury stock method.  The Warrants became exercisable at the election of the holders on January&#160;15, 2021, and as a result, they were included as potentially dilutive securities on an adjusted weighted-average basis for the portion of the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2021, for which they were outstanding.  A majority of the Warrants were exercised during the second quarter of 2021, and the remaining outstanding Warrants were dilutive during the three months ended September&#160;30, 2022, and 2021, and the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2022, as presented below.  Please refer to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 3 - Equity &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 7 - Compensation Plans &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;in this report, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 9 - Earnings Per Share&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; in the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;&lt;a href="http://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/893538/000089353822000020/sm-20211231.htm" style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"&gt;2021 Form 10-K&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt; for additional detail on these potentially dilutive securities.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;When the Company recognizes a net loss from continuing operations, all potentially dilutive shares are anti-dilutive and are consequently excluded from the calculation of diluted net loss per common share.     <us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock
      contextRef="i3b79dc1c07344b1a997ff668145f5bfb_D20220101-20220930"
      id="id3VybDovL2RvY3MudjEvZG9jOmFjYzhhN2Q0N2IxZDQ5NmY4ZWJkNzQ5OTc3YzBjNGY5L3NlYzphY2M4YTdkNDdiMWQ0OTZmOGViZDc0OTk3N2MwYzRmOV83Ni9mcmFnOmExODQwMDBlNmNiNjQ0MjI4YTFjNWNjYjFkZTRiZjZlL3RleHRyZWdpb246YTE4NDAwMGU2Y2I2NDQyMjhhMWM1Y2NiMWRlNGJmNmVfNjEyMw_4fba4251-73b4-4d4c-8277-e811a7603b98">&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%"&gt;Note 10 - Derivative Financial Instruments&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Summary of Oil, Gas, and NGL Derivative Contracts in Place&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company regularly enters into commodity derivative contracts to mitigate a portion of its exposure to oil, gas, and NGL price volatility and location differentials, and the associated impact on cash flows.  As of September&#160;30, 2022, all contracts were entered into for other-than-trading purposes.  The Company&#x2019;s commodity derivative contracts consist of price swap and collar arrangements for oil, gas, and NGL production.  In a typical commodity swap agreement, if the agreed upon published third-party index price (&#x201c;index price&#x201d;) is lower than the swap price, the Company receives the difference between the index price and the agreed upon swap price.  If the index price is higher than the swap price, the Company pays the difference.  For collar arrangements, the Company receives the difference between an agreed upon index price and the floor price if the index price is below the floor price.  The Company pays the difference between the agreed upon ceiling price and the index price if the index price is above the ceiling price.  No amounts are paid or received if the index price is between the floor and ceiling prices.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company has entered into fixed price oil and gas basis swaps in order to mitigate exposure to adverse pricing differentials between certain industry benchmark prices and the actual physical pricing points where the Company&#x2019;s production is sold.  As of September&#160;30, 2022, the Company has basis swap contracts with fixed price differentials between:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;padding-left:54pt;text-indent:-18pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.85pt"&gt;NYMEX WTI and WTI Midland for a portion of its Midland Basin oil production with sales contracts that settle at WTI Midland prices;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;padding-left:54pt;text-indent:-18pt"&gt;&lt;span Brent&#x201d;) for a portion of its Midland Basin oil production with sales contracts that settle at ICE Brent prices;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;padding-left:54pt;text-indent:-18pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:14.85pt"&gt;NYMEX WTI and Argus WTI Houston Magellan East Houston Terminal (&#x201c;MEH&#x201d;) for a portion of its South Texas oil production with sales contracts that settle at Argus WTI Houston MEH (&#x201c;WTI Houston MEH&#x201d;) prices;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;padding-left:54pt;text-indent:-18pt"&gt;&lt;span of its Midland Basin gas production with sales contracts that settle at IF Waha prices; and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:6pt;padding-left:54pt;text-indent:-18pt"&gt;&lt;span portion of its South Texas gas production with sales contracts that settle at IF HSC prices.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;The Company has also entered into oil swap contracts to fix the differential in pricing between the NYMEX calendar month average and the physical crude oil delivery month (&#x201c;Roll Differential&#x201d;) in which the Company pays the periodic variable Roll Differential and receives a weighted-average fixed price differential.  The weighted-average fixed price differential represents the amount of net addition (reduction) to delivery month prices for the notional volumes covered by the swap contracts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;As of style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;Offsetting of Derivative Assets and Liabilities&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"&gt;As of September&#160;30, 2022, and December&#160;31, 2021, all derivative instruments held by the Company were subject to master netting arrangements with various financial institutions.  In general, the terms of the Company&#x2019;s agreements provide for offsetting of amounts payable or receivable between it and the counterparty, at the election of both parties, for transactions that settle on the same date and in the same currency.  The Company&#x2019;s agreements also provide that in the event of an early termination, the counterparties have the right to offset amounts owed or owing under that and any other agreement with the same counterparty.  The Company&#x2019;s accounting policy is to not offset these positions in its accompanying balance sheets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="margin-bottom:12pt;text-indent:36pt"&gt;&lt;span
